clue.text: Reserve champion gets the record

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: The runner-up at a show is handed the trophy's record book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve champion' looks like one show-ring title, but 'Reserve' is the definition and 'champion' a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of work or orders held over for later is a stock kept in hand, a reserve.

clue.text: Old codger used to stop the train

explanation.surface: An elderly man pulls the communication cord.
explanation.definitionFit: An old buffer is a slang name for a fusty elderly man; railway buffers are the sprung pads that absorb a train's impact and halt it.

clue.text: It's said to create something rotten

indicators.note: the clue tells us a spoken phrase is meant, so the word sounded out is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to create, in informal British speech, is to make a fuss, as is to carry on

explanation.surface: Gossip is supposed to stir up something nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Create' here is the British colloquial verb for making a scene, a meaning also covered by 'carry on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead and decaying flesh, as eaten by crows, is putrid matter.

clue.text: Liking law cases where guilt is uncertain.I love being entertained

indicators.note: a guest being entertained is taken in, so these letters are held inside the jumble
something uncertain is unsettled, so the letters of guilt and is are jumbled up

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A guilty verdict is in doubt; someone confesses to enjoying the fun of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liking law cases' is the definition, though 'law cases' could seem to start the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person fond of going to court sues readily, keen on lawsuits and legal disputes.

clue.text: Outside store, someone catching insect

indicators.note: the word placed outside wraps around the other piece, here the shop

parts.note: one who catches or seizes things is a grasper
a shop is a store

explanation.surface: Outside a shop, a person grabs a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside store' reads as a location in the surface, but 'Outside' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasshopper is a leaping, chirping creature of meadows, one example of the class of six-legged bugs.

clue.text: Recover lost ground — what a sauce!

explanation.surface: Someone praises a condiment while making up a lost lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up a deficit is to draw level with others; catchup is a variant spelling of ketchup, the tomato condiment.

clue.text: Rod and line, as the saying goes

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is spoken out loud, so a word heard the same is wanted

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: An angler's rod and line, as people like to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod and line' suggests fishing; 'Rod' is a billiard stick and 'line' the waiting row.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is the long tapered stick used to strike balls in snooker or billiards.

clue.text: Kid drinks one over the eight

annotationWithheld.why: Kid drinks one over the eight (5) for TEASE: TEAS for drinks leaves E, and no reading of 'one over the eight' gives E without a word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Kid drinks one over the eight

clue.text: Source of water that's hard -try and put in order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: letters put in order are rearranged into a new sequence, so try and is reworked

explanation.surface: A tap that delivers hard water needs sorting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in order' rearranges TRY AND into YDRANT, after H.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire hydrant is a street outlet from the mains that firefighters tap for supply.

clue.text: Exchange cash for leverage

explanation.surface: Swapping money for influence.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy something is to hand over money for it; purchase also means a firm grip or mechanical advantage.

clue.text: Putting pies back in to bake? That's excellent

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another, the reversed pies going into the baking word

parts.note: to fire is to bake pottery in a kiln

indicators.note: putting something back reverses it, so the word for pies is read the other way round

parts.note: tarts are pies

explanation.surface: Someone returns pies to the oven and pronounces them splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TARTS into STRAT, which goes 'in' FIRE: FIR-STRAT-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the top class is outstanding, superb.

clue.text: Creature seen in summer

explanation.surface: A snake spotted during the warm months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is read as one who sums, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: An adder is Britain's only venomous snake; an adder is also one who adds figures, a summer.

clue.text: Regarding an investment of money in gilts

indicators.note: something invested is put inside, so the answer lies within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A remark about putting cash into government bonds.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilts are British government bonds; the answer runs through monEY IN Gilts.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at something closely is watching or considering it.

clue.text: Englishman in the band hits back

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the band, as the clue places it

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder

indicators.note: hits read back means the synonym is reversed

parts.note: to cane is to hit, so canes means hits

explanation.surface: An Englishman playing in a group strikes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CANES into SENAC, which goes 'in' SASH. 'band' suggests a music group.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassenach is a Scots term, often derogatory, for a person from south of the border.

clue.text: Still without a chance to recover quickly

parts.note: a snap is a still photograph
a contender who is out of it has no chance of winning

explanation.surface: Even lacking an opportunity, someone bounces back fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is a noun, a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake off a mood or daze abruptly is to regain composure at once.

clue.text: In the train, father's in charge of the kids

parts.note: a loco, short for locomotive, is the engine of a train
father's read as father is, and a father is a parent, so parent is

explanation.surface: Dad is looking after the children on the train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'father's' is the contraction 'father is', giving PARENT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means acting in place of a parent, as a teacher with responsibility for pupils.

clue.text: Short-term soldiers trapped in river, being unprepared

indicators.note: things trapped in another are held inside it, so the temp and soldiers sit within the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
a temp is a short-term worker
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Temporary troops are stuck in a river with no preparation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-term' looks like an adjective on 'soldiers' but gives TEMP alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Done on the spur of the moment, without notes or rehearsal, is improvised.

clue.text: Backed donkey is Neddy

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
Neddy and Ted are both pet forms of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A claim that a donkey is called Neddy has been supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neddy' suggests a donkey, but it is a pet name for Edward, as Ted is.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or help someone is to back them.

clue.text: Independent plunges profits into reorganisation

indicators.note: a reorganisation shuffles things into a new order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An independent firm sinks its earnings into restructuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reorganisation' rearranges PLUNGES PROFITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to pay one's own way without outside help is to be self-reliant.

clue.text: Leaves Latvian money over

parts.note: a Lett is a Latvian

indicators.note: in a down clue the word turned over is read upwards, reversing it

parts.note: the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro

explanation.surface: Latvian cash is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the salad noun; the ecu was the pre-euro European unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a plant grown for its green foliage eaten in salads.

clue.text: Scrooge nearly, nearly, bore up

indicators.note: nearly means almost all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nigh means nearly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a drag is a bore, something tedious

explanation.surface: Scrooge almost endured something, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'nearly' trims NIGH to NIG; 'up' turns DRAG to GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge, in Dickens, is the classic miser, a stingy person.

clue.text: Eccentric sailors on board steam yacht

indicators.note: people on board a ship are inside it, so the sailors go within the vessel's letters

parts.note: SY is the standard abbreviation for steam yacht in ships' names
the crew are the sailors of a ship

explanation.surface: Odd sailors are aboard a steam-powered yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwy is slang for odd or crazy.

clue.text: Render in palindromic form

annotationWithheld.why: Render in palindromic form (9) for INTERPRET: IN plus TERPRET, a seven-letter palindrome that is no word, which the grammar cannot build from the clue words

clue.text: A problem concerning transport

parts.note: re is a word meaning concerning, as in business letters
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: A difficulty about getting around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words, a brain-teaser.

clue.text: Soldier wearing coat with amazing properties

indicators.note: the soldier wears the coat, so the coat is around him

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a remarkable coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic describes something enchanted, having supernatural power.

clue.text: General practitioner following in this way shortly

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the other
said shortly, the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: thus means in this way
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a qualified medical practitioner

explanation.surface: A family doctor coming after, briefly, in this manner.
explanation.walkthrough: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of a famous small showman in P. T. Barnum's circus. 'General practitioner' reads as one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Thumb, the diminutive performer, carried the mock rank of general.

clue.text: Sort of faucets to stop the flow of air

definitions.text: to stop the flow of air

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of tap that cuts off the air supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like 'a kind of', but 'Sort' alone rearranges OF FAUCETS.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother or choke something is to deprive it of breath.

clue.text: Sprinter is racing the leaders for the title

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters

parts.note: the letters running backwards through Sprinter is are a coincidence; only the leading letters are used

explanation.surface: A runner is competing to win the championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the honorific given to a knight, a form of address.

clue.text: Storage unit employed in the theatre

explanation.surface: A cupboard used backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a kitchen sideboard with shelves; in theatre a dresser helps actors with costumes.

clue.text: Twenty-four hours of special sea duty

indicators.note: special suggests something altered from the usual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A day's extra watch at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges SEA DUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekday is one day, a full day and night.
